newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends down on soft cash, mild weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends down on soft cash, mild weather.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended lower across the board Friday in a lackluster session, after some pre-weekend short covering gave way to more selling amid mostly-bearish fundamentals, industry sources said.
March slipped 3.3 cents to close at $1.966 per million British thermal units after hitting $2.05 earlier. April settled 4.1 cents lower at $1.95. Others also ended lower.
"There's nothing bullish in the forecast. It just melted down at the end when there were no bids to support it," said one East Coast trader, noting cash was weaker today.
NYMEX will be closed Monday for Presidents' Day holiday.
With mostly seasonal to above-seasonal U.S. weather expected next week and inventories comfortable, most traders saw little hope for a significant rally near-term.

And while technical traders said the market was oversold and could bounce, most agreed the underlying trend was still bearish, particularly after March's break this week below key support and through a trendline. They pegged next support at $1.905, the bottom of the continuation gap, and then at the contract low of t $1.749. Resistance was seen first near $2.10 and then in the $2.25-2.30 area.

On the physical side, Gulf Coast prices fell another 10 cents to the $2.10-2.15 range. Midcontinent pipes were 10-15 cents lower at around $1.90. New York city gate gas slumped more than 15 cents to about the $2.60 level.
The 12-month strip fell 1.2 cents to $2.049. NYMEX said an estimated 24,247 Hub contracts traded, down sharply from Thursday's revised tally of 49,713. NYMEX March Hub natgas expires Monday, Feb 24.
No NYMEX Permian or Alberta contracts traded Friday.
On the KCBT, March finished two cents lower at $1.72, while deferreds ended down by one to 3.5 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.7 cent to 24.6 cents (NYMEX premium).
Permian physicals softened by another 25 cents to the low-$1.80s.
